learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of materials technology, understanding the relationship between processing, structure, and properties for different materials.

Have adequate knowledge of materials technology, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field in mechanical engineering, to develop advanced technologies in fields relating processing, structure, and properties.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering, opening up the concepts of materials technology for their subsequent relationship with other fields.

Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve materials technology problems using established methods, explaining the behavior of materials in different work fields.
Be able to design and conduct materials technology experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory competencies in materials technology.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve materials technology problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in materials technology and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
An understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: Main forming methods for metallic, ceramic, and polymeric materials. Effect on microstructure and properties
Metals. Melting and casting of metallic materials. Microstructural development.
Metals. Fundamentals of plastic deformation forming.
Welding. Defects. Inspection and non-destructive testing.
Powder Technology. Processing of Ceramic Materials.
In-service behavior of materials: creep, fatigue, fracture, corrosion and wear.
Surface treatments. Improvement of component in-service behavior.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (tests, classroom work, laboratory practices)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of a final exam (60%) and continuous assessment (40%). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained on the final exam for the continuous assessment grade to be counted. Mandatory attendance and completion of laboratory practices are required to be evaluated in the course. Failure to attend laboratories without justified cause implies failing the continuous assessment.
